Unknown.); the IA full text is a single text stream with no page markers and the OCR has damaged digits and superscripts (for example the W/E index printed as 3 *5-3'9), so only the legible items are recorded here.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body colour cannot be determined because the old dry specimens are faded; presumably similar to T. rapulum. Posterior margin of the head capsule less than a semicircle behind the eyes, slightly undulate immediately behind the eyes; fontanelle distinct, Y-shaped, the lateral arms long, reaching almost half the distance to the ocellus, slender but slightly swollen where they end in other species; frons with two branching depressions in front of the fontanelle, or the two joined; eyes very short, oval, moderately projecting relative to their own diameter but small relative to the head width, the ratio of head width to eye length 3.5—3.9; ocelli medium-sized, their distance from the eye more than half and up to more than three-quarters of their own shortest diameter; postclypeus moderately to strongly inflated, 2.1—2.4 times as wide as long, anterior margin slightly concave, posterior margin convex and rounded, slightly arched in the middle; molar plate of the right mandible with 7—8 ridges; antennae 15-segmented, segments 2, 4 and 5 about equal in length, segments 3 and 6 about equal to each other and slightly longer than those; the pale odoriferous patch on the anterior margin of abdominal sternite 5 small; cerci about as long as their basal width, slightly papilliform. Pilosity of the vertex unequal in length, not forming felt or a pad. Measurements (1 locality, 10 individuals): head width (including the eyes) 1.61—1.76 mm (mean 1.66), maximum diameter of the eye 0.43—0.48 mm (0.46), ocellus 0.16—0.18×0.20—0.25 mm (0.17×0.22), ocellus to eye 0.10—0.13 mm (0.11), pronotal width 1.38—1.61 mm (1.48), pronotal length 0.84—0.94 mm (0.90), length of the hind tibia 2.04—2.24 mm (2.17), length of the anterior wing 15.50—16.30 mm (15.73).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: It differs from T. dispar and T. rapulum in the relatively smaller eyes, the ocelli farther from the eyes and the shorter cerci; apart from the cerci, the same characters distinguish it from T. togoensis and T. occidentalis. The lateral arms of the fontanelle spread widely to the sides, which differs from every other Trinervitermes except certain T. trinervoides. Only the alate is known; the soldier is unknown.
